q: Which investigation is most helpful in assessing a child with an acute asthma attack?
o: Arterial blood gas in every child
e: Pulse oximetry is the best bedside test of severity.

q: The most significant risk factor for childhood asthma is:
e: Atopy and parental asthma are the strongest risk factors.

q: In acute severe asthma, all are true EXCEPT:
e: A severe attack has a peak flow of 50% or less; a life-threatening attack has a peak flow below 33%.
Little air moves, so the wheeze disappears.

q: All are chest X-ray findings in asthma EXCEPT:
e: Hyperinflation is typical; the heart is normal.

q: In an acute attack, a normal or rising PaCO₂ means:
o: The child is tiring and needs intensive care
e: Early in an attack the PaCO₂ is low; a normal PaCO₂ is a danger sign that the child is tiring.

q: A 16-year-old known to have asthma is short of breath. Which feature suggests severe asthma?
e: Pulsus paradoxus of more than 10–20 mmHg indicates severe obstruction.

q: According to GINA 2026, a 9-year-old with asthma symptoms twice a week should receive:
o: A treatment that contains an inhaled corticosteroid, not salbutamol alone
e: Treatment with a short-acting beta-agonist alone is no longer advised for children aged 6–11 years.
k: not be treated with salbutamol alone

q: Before stepping up treatment in a poorly controlled asthmatic child, the first thing to check is:
e: Most poor control is due to technique, adherence or triggers.

q: A 7-year-old in a severe asthma attack has not improved after salbutamol, ipratropium and intravenous hydrocortisone. What is the next drug?
e: Magnesium sulphate 40 mg/kg (maximum 2 g) over 20 minutes.

q: A child with asthma on inhaled fluticasone develops white plaques in the mouth. What is the advice?
o: Use a spacer and rinse the mouth after each dose
e: Oral thrush from inhaled corticosteroids is reduced by a spacer and rinsing the mouth.

q: The best device for a 2-year-old with asthma is:
o: Metered-dose inhaler with a spacer and face mask
e: At 0–3 years: a metered-dose inhaler with a spacer and a face mask.
